article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: Grapefruit female × Blueberry male
Breeder: Electric Seed Company
THC Content: 22%
CBD Content: Not officially documented
Terpene Profile: myrcene , limonene , caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Blueberry, mixed berries, grapefruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 58 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September
Indoor Yield: 100 g (3 oz.) per large plant
Outdoor Yield: 275 g (10 oz.) per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Blue Grape is an old Canadian cannabis hybrid whose name describes its flavor far better than many modern strain names do. Originally released as Blue Grape #1 by Electric Seed Company, the cultivar combines a stout Grapefruit female with a vigorous Blueberry male, producing weed that brings together two of the fruitiest genetic families available during its era. The original description preserved in Ed Rosenthal ‘s The Big Book of Buds, Volume 2 classifies the plant as 70% indica yet emphasizes an alert, energetic, head-oriented high rather than a sleepy body stone.

Its flowers carry a full berry flavor sharpened by tangy grapefruit, while wide dark foliage can acquire blue-purple coloration as maturity approaches. Electric Seed Company also selected the cross for practical garden performance, giving it a moderate 58-day indoor flowering period and a late-September outdoor harvest. Although the cultivar is more accurately called Blue Grape #1 in historical references, the shorter Blue Grape name is commonly used when discussing this original Grapefruit × Blueberry hybrid.
Genetics and Lineage

Electric Seed Company created Blue Grape #1 by pollinating a stout, bushy Grapefruit female with a Blueberry male chosen specifically for vigor and hardiness. Both parental lines were associated with the Pacific Northwest cannabis scene and had already developed reputations for unusual fruit flavors and distinctive effects. Historical lineage records independently preserve the same Grapefruit × Blueberry pedigree and identify Electric Seed Company as the breeder, making this one of the better-documented older Blueberry-family crosses.

Blueberry contributes much more than berry flavor. Classic Blueberry genetics are rooted in DJ Short ‘s work with Thai, Oaxaca -influenced, and Afghani cannabis populations, creating plants capable of producing dark coloration, broad leaves, resinous flowers, fruit aromas, and a combination of cerebral and physical effects. Grapefruit pushes the cross toward a brighter, sharper direction with citrus character and a more energetic mental quality. In Blue Grape, the resulting 70/30 indica-sativa balance produces compact-looking foliage and substantial branching while retaining a high that feels far more lively than the indica percentage might suggest.

The cultivar should not be confused with Blue Grape Dream, Blue Grape Fuel, or newer dispensary strains using the Blue Grape name. Blue Grape Dream is a later GreenLabel Seeds hybrid that also happens to combine Blueberry and Grapefruit, while Blue Grape Fuel carries an entirely different Animal Cookies, HeadStash, Northern Lights #5 , and Blueberry lineage. The historically documented Blue Grape #1 is the Electric Seed Company version described here.
Effects and Experience

Blue Grape challenges the assumption that indica-dominant marijuana must produce a sleepy experience. Electric Seed Company’s original description characterizes the high as alert and energizing, with a predominantly head-focused quality well suited to daytime activity. The first stage may bring an upbeat shift in mood, greater interest in conversation, and enough mental stimulation for hobbies, errands, music, or relaxed creative work. The effect tends to feel buoyant rather than aggressively racy, which gives the cultivar a useful middle ground between highly stimulating sativa weed and physically heavy indica varieties.

As the session continues, the Blueberry side can add a softer physical undertone. Muscles may loosen and the overall pace becomes more comfortable, yet moderate servings typically preserve motivation and mental clarity. That quality was specifically highlighted in early descriptions, which praised the strain for delivering an awake experience despite its indica-dominant genetic classification. Larger doses can naturally make the high more introspective and less functional, particularly in consumers with limited tolerance.

There is no defensible universal THC number for the original Electric Seed Company release. Modern sources sometimes assign percentages to similarly named strains, but those values should not be retroactively applied to an older seed line without laboratory evidence. Potency should therefore be judged from testing of the actual flower whenever available.
Medical Benefits

The clear, active nature of Blue Grape historically made it attractive to medical marijuana consumers looking for relief without giving up motivation. The original strain description specifically noted potential pain reduction while preserving mental clarity and energy. That combination may be appealing to people who find heavily sedating weed impractical during daytime hours. Cannabis with a similar effect profile is sometimes chosen when temporary stress, mild physical discomfort, reduced motivation, or tension interfere with normal activity.

Those traditional uses do not establish Blue Grape as a clinically proven treatment. No controlled medical trials have evaluated the cultivar itself, and its cannabinoid composition was never standardized. Individual consumers can also respond very differently to THC-containing cannabis. Larger amounts may produce dizziness, impaired coordination, anxiety, or unwanted mental fog even when moderate amounts feel clear and energizing.

Medical consumers should therefore treat strain history as general guidance rather than a substitute for product testing or professional advice. The chemical analysis of the specific flower is more meaningful than assumptions based solely on the Blue Grape name.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Flavor is where the two parents interact most obviously. Electric Seed Company described the smoke as smooth, with a full berry character followed by tangy grapefruit. Blueberry sweetness tends to provide the foundation, suggesting ripe berries, berry skin, and dark fruit, while Grapefruit contributes a sharper citrus edge that prevents the profile from becoming overly sweet.

Breaking apart cured flowers can reveal more traditional cannabis notes beneath the fruit. Mild earth, herbs, resin, and spice may accompany the berry-citrus core, particularly in plants leaning toward the Blueberry side. The result differs considerably from today’s grape-candy cultivars. Blue Grape is fruity, but the sweetness remains natural and botanical rather than resembling syrup or artificial flavoring.

No standardized terpene analysis was published for the original cultivar. Limonene would be compatible with its grapefruit character, myrcene could contribute berry and earthy depth, while caryophyllene and pinene may account for spice and herbal sharpness. These are plausible sensory associations rather than verified strain-wide chemistry, and individual harvests should be laboratory tested before assigning dominant terpenes.
Growing Information

Blue Grape was deliberately selected as an approachable garden plant. The original breeder material describes plants that prefer to become fairly large and develop numerous flowering sites rather than concentrating production entirely into one cola. Broad, dark leaves reinforce the indica appearance, and certain individuals develop attractive blue-purple pigmentation. Glossy resin forms across the plants as flowering progresses, with enough trichome coverage that the breeder specifically mentioned producing dense finger hash from resin collected from the foliage.

Branch support becomes important late in bloom. Electric Seed Company recommended tying larger side branches as the flowers gain weight, both to prevent them from bending and to maintain an orderly canopy. Modern growers can accomplish the same objective with stakes, a support net, or low-stress training begun earlier in development. The natural multi-site growth pattern makes the strain particularly suitable for a broad canopy where several branches receive strong light.

Indoor flowering is approximately 58 days, placing Blue Grape close to an eight-week schedule. Original yield figures were approximately 100 grams, or three ounces, per large indoor plant. Outdoors, the breeder listed roughly 275 grams, or ten ounces, per plant with harvest arriving in late September. Those figures reflect the cultivation standards and techniques of the strain’s original era and should not be treated as hard biological limits. Modern lighting, larger root systems, training, and environmental control could change production considerably.

The relatively early outdoor finish is a valuable characteristic in temperate climates. Late September maturity reduces exposure to the prolonged autumn rain that threatens many October- and November-finishing marijuana strains . Dense flower sites should still receive adequate airflow, particularly where cool nighttime humidity becomes common near harvest.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Blue Grape?
The original Blue Grape #1 from Electric Seed Company is Grapefruit × Blueberry. The breeder used a stout Grapefruit female and a vigorous, hardy Blueberry male.
Is Blue Grape indica or sativa?

Blue Grape #1 is approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa. Despite that indica-dominant classification, its original breeder description emphasizes an alert, energizing, head-focused high rather than heavy sedation.
What does Blue Grape taste like?

The original cultivar combines a full sweet berry flavor with tangy grapefruit. Blueberry, mixed berries, sweet fruit, citrus peel, mild earth, and herbs may all appear depending on phenotype and curing.
How long does Blue Grape take to flower?
Electric Seed Company listed approximately 58 days of indoor flowering. Outdoors, Blue Grape #1 was expected to finish around late September.
Who bred the original Blue Grape strain?

Electric Seed Company bred the historical Blue Grape #1. The strain was distributed through the Canadian cannabis seed market and is documented in The Big Book of Buds, Volume 2 as an Electric Seed Company variety.
Final Thoughts on Blue Grape

Blue Grape is a useful reminder that fruit-forward cannabis did not begin with the modern dessert-strain era. Electric Seed Company paired Grapefruit with Blueberry decades ago and produced a cultivar whose identity genuinely revolved around the flavors named in its pedigree. Sweet berry and tangy citrus accompany dark foliage, occasional purple-blue coloration, abundant resin, and a surprisingly active high for a 70% indica hybrid.

Its practical traits strengthen the historical appeal. Approximately 58 days of indoor flowering, late-September outdoor maturity, straightforward branching, and respectable production made Blue Grape #1 accessible to ordinary growers rather than only specialists. The need to support heavy lateral branches is a manageable tradeoff for a plant naturally inclined to develop numerous productive flowering sites.

Most importantly, the original strain should be distinguished from the several newer cultivars now carrying similar names. The historically documented Blue Grape is Electric Seed Company’s Grapefruit × Blueberry hybrid—a berry-rich, citrus-edged piece of Canadian cannabis breeding whose daytime-friendly effects and old-school fruit profile still give it a recognizable identity.
